messages:
incbot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: Smart-routing fallback loop detected for capacity-tier routing (hosted->dedicated). Trigger: rate of spillage to dedicated pools > 500 req/min, errors from dedicated: 503/tenant isolation violations. Pager: @alice.nguyen on-call.

alice.nguyen: seeing sustained error rate on /v1/generate for several hosted customers -- we've got spillover into dedicated and dedicated nodes are returning tenant-isolation rejections. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/infra/routing/spillover – CPU on dedicated is normal but logs show lots of rejected tokens with tenant mismatch.

mike.chen: confirmed. fallbackPolicy for region eu-west-1 had "allow_spillover: true" and prioritized dedicated variant for fallback. Someone flipped the policy during yesterday's rollout. That causes hosted traffic to be routed into dedicated capacity for some tenants.

sara_ops: oh no. That explains the tenant-isolation errors — requests are carrying hosted tenant headers but landing on dedicated pools that enforce isolation. We need immediate mitigation: disable cross-tier fallback and route to secondary hosted variants.

alice.nguyen: agreed. quick mitigation plan: 1) disable cross-tier fallback policy 2) add short-term soft-fail (503->200 stub) to hosted clients so we don't overload dedicated 3) notify affected enterprise customers. Who can flip policy now?

mike.chen: I can patch the routing config in the control plane. Will do a guarded change: set fallbackPolicy.allow_spillover=false for the eu-west-1 routing group and set a canary to 1% for 5m. Command: 
```bash
# set policy via control-plane API
curl -X PATCH https://control-plane.internal/v1/routing/groups/eu-west-1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"fallbackPolicy": {"allow_spillover": false}}'
```
I'll push now and monitor.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: config-change started by mike.chen (routing-group: eu-west-1) — config-change-id: cfg-20240304-01

alice.nguyen: monitoring logs and metrics. alerting thresholds lowered. please post status updates every 2m.

mike.chen: rolled the change. config-change-id cfg-20240304-01 applied. Canary at 0.1 -> 1% -> 10% -> paused at 100%. Observing metrics...

mike.chen: initial drop in spillover, dedicated rejection rate down 80%. However we're seeing a small loop where some requests are still being retried and hitting the region fallback which tries next available variant and picks dedicated again. Need to also disable cross-region fallback for affected tenants temporarily.

alice.nguyen: can we add a short-circuit in the router to honor tenant_deployment_type preference? Example: prefer_hosted=true for non-enterprise or if dedicated target tenant mismatch. Short term rule: reject if target pool tenant != request tenant.

mike.chen: adding rule now. patch: 
```json
{"routingHints": {"prefer_hosted": true, "enforce_tenant_strictness": true}}
```
Applying...

devops-bot: deploy-bot: routing rule update applied by mike.chen — change-id rr-20240304-11

alice.nguyen: good, rejection rate down to negligible. Spillover stop looks stable. Still seeing about 12 affected customers with intermittent 503s during the window.

support-bot: Auto-gather: affected_customers: ["acme-corp","fastchat-ai","shopzoom"], windows: 5m-25m UTC. Generated impact digest ticket #INC-20240304-182.

alice.nguyen: preparing customer-facing note. Short summary: we had a misconfigured fallback policy that caused hosted traffic to be routed into dedicated pools for a subset of tenants, leading to tenant isolation rejections and elevated errors. Root cause fix: disabled cross-tier spillover + tightened tenant strictness in routing.

ben.data: taking over on-call for the next shift. Handoff: current status: mitigation applied, spillover stopped, dedicated pools stable, 12 customers impacted with transient 4xx/5xx during 00:05-00:30 UTC. Next actions: run full audit of fallbackPolicy changes in last 72h, roll back the policy change that enabled allow_spillover if it was intentional and recreate a safer canary, run integration tests for tenant header enforcement, and prepare postmortem.

alice.nguyen: thanks Ben. Handing off monitoring dashboards and logs links: https://console.redwood/alerts/INC-20240304-182 and link to routing change cfg-20240304-01 and rr-20240304-11.

ben.data: I'll also coordinate with product and sales for customer outreach. Suggest message: "We identified a routing policy configuration that briefly routed traffic into customers' dedicated capacity causing failed requests; we've reverted the change and applied stricter routing rules to prevent recurrence. We're running a full audit and will follow up."

mike.chen: +1. I'll prepare a small hotfix to disallow cross-tier as default and add an explicit opt-in for planned spillovers. Also adding unit/integration tests in routing service for tenant fingerprint checks. ETA for PR: 4h.

alice.nguyen: Customer impact assessment: non-critical (no data exposure), availability blip for certain hosted endpoints, SLOs impacted for a small set of enterprise tenants for ~25 minutes. Recommend severity = Sev2.

ben.data: scheduling postmortem for today 16:00 UTC. Assignments: mike -> config change and tests; alice -> incident timeline and monitoring runbook updates; sara_ops -> customer comms draft; infra -> audit logs.

devops-bot: reminder: please escalate to oncall-manager if you need org-level notifications > 30 minutes.

support-bot: created customer notes draft: "We experienced a service disruption affecting request routing for a small number of customers between 00:05-00:30 UTC. The issue was caused by a routing configuration change and has been mitigated. No customer data was exposed. We're following up with a post-incident report."

alice.nguyen: thanks everyone. marking thread as incident-active -> monitoring. Ben, you're primary oncall. If anything regresses ping me or escalate. :thumbsup:

ben.data: acknowledged, taking over. I'll post the postmortem link once ready.
